title: Cryptographic proof-of-possession and operations play for SSO/RBAC/KMS
creator: Sofia Lee
description: This PRD defines the minimum technical and operational requirements to prove cryptographic possession of keys (customer and operator), the runbook for KMS escrow and recovery validation, and the evidence collection procedures for SSO/SAML assertions and RBAC policy enforcement in Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. The goal is to produce an auditable package that satisfies enterprise compliance teams and enables a standardized sign-off across Security, Ops, and Legal. The scope includes operator certification steps, automated verification scripts, acceptance sampling criteria, and post-rollout monitoring requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Customer key proof-of-possession flow demonstrated for at-rest and in-transit keys using challenge-response within a dedicated test tenant
Operator managed key workflows (rotate, revoke, escrow retrieval) executed end-to-end without losing customer-encrypted objects in a staged recovery test
SSO/SAML federation replay and expiry tests validated; assertion revocation observed in downstream services within configured propagation SLA (<= 60s)
RBAC policy matrix applied to a representative set of resources; least-privilege violations flagged and resolved in automated policy evaluation
Immutable audit logs collected for all KMS operations, SSO assertion events, and RBAC changes for a 30-day test window; checksum verification passes and retention policy enforcement confirmed
Runbook signed by Security, Ops, and Legal with checklist items ticked and artifact links provided
decisions: Adopt HSM-backed keys for operator escrow keys in on-prem tenants where customer requires FIPS-like assurance
Use challenge-response (signed nonce) as canonical proof-of-possession for both customer and operator keys rather than distributing raw key material
Require per-tenant audit bundles (WORM) exported to customer-owned S3/GCS for regulated customers — default retention 90 days configurable
Federation rollback will use assertion blacklisting + session revocation endpoint; fallback to short session TTL for older integrations
checklist: Design: Detailed dataflow diagram for proof-of-possession and escrow retrieval (design doc link below)
Engineering: Implement challenge-response API + model tests for key verification
Security: Threat model review completed and signed
Ops: Runbook drafted with step-by-step recovery and escalation contacts
Legal: SLA language for key custody and escrow responsibilities approved
QA: End-to-end rehearsals of key rotation and escrow recovery 3 times across two regions
Compliance: Sample audit evidence packaged and validated against SOC2 checklist
Console: New artifacts (operator-cert status, audit export controls) surfaced in Console UI for private deployments
notes: We intentionally separate proof-of-possession from escrow retrieval to avoid accidental key material exposure during audits.
Operator certification will be time-boxed: initial certification window = 2 weeks of monitored operations after training
This PRD focuses on Private deployments; Hosted customers will get a simplified variant (no operator escrow unless requested)

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Operator key compromise could allow unauthorized escrow retrieval — Mitigation: HSM-backed operator keys + split custody + periodic key ceremonies
Risk: Assertion revocation propagation slower than SLA — Mitigation: add push-based session revoke endpoint and fall back to short session TTL
Risk: Audit exports could accidentally include PII — Mitigation: scrub tool runs before export and legal review per-customer
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): Run PoP and escrow rehearsal in isolated test tenants for 2 customers (internal and external pilot)
Stage 2 (beta): Expose operator-cert and escrow features to 10 private tenants with Security oversight for 60 days
Stage 3 (GA): Enable default tooling in private deployments; update onboarding checklist and Console UI
